source_review.note: Asaveri is {arohana} ascending and {avarohana} descending. Neither Wikipedia surface has it: the list page gives {scraped} and the article {article}, and those two differ from each other in one note only, which is why the raga carries a recorded disagreement at all. The reviewer's reading differs from both in three places - the interior Shadja is the upper one, the Madhyama-Panchama pair is the other way round, and the Rishabha before the Gandhara is not there. The first of those three the sthayi solver derives independently from the run's own shape, which is the part of this verdict that is not taken on trust. The arohana is unchanged from both surfaces and is recorded anyway so a re-scrape cannot break it. Both surfaces' avarohanas are kept as alternatives rather than discarded: each is defensible, and the page should show the disagreement instead of hiding it behind one chosen reading. Both are recorded with the interior Shadja as the upper one, which is the single correction they and the reviewer agree on. Keeping the article's alternative also gives the raga's declared anya swara - a Rishabha the reviewer's reading does not use - a note in the data that actually uses it.
